full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J. This application for review arises out of the judgment and order 02.11.2009 passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 240 of 2009 dismissing the same and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 26.11.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 10220 of 2007 making the Rule absolute and thereby setting aside the order No. 60 dated 28.10.2007 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Bogra in Money Execution Case No. 142 of 2000 allowing the application  filed under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and thereby setting aside the auction sale dated 18.08.2005. 

 3. The decree holder Agrani Bank filed Artha Rin Case No. 49 of 1997 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Bogra, for realization of Tk.13,34,503,62/- due from the judgment-debtor-petitioner. On 26.05.1998, the suit was decreed ex parte in preliminary form which was made final on 03.06.1999. In order to satisfy the decree, the decree holder bank filed Execution Case No. 142 of 2000. In compliance with the previsions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and under direction of the Execution Court, a notice for auction sale of the mortgaged property was published in two daily newspapers. On 08.08.2005, the judgment-debtor-petitioner entered appearance in the execution case and prayed for adjournment of the auction sale with a plea of compromise. The Executing Court allowed time fixing 11.08.2005 for filing petition for compromise   but the judgment-debtor-petitioner did not file the required compromise and hence the Execution Court fixed 18.08.2005 for auction and on that date, the auction purchaser-respondent No. 1 participated in the bid and his bid, being the highest, was accepted. Accordingly, he deposited 25% of the hid money on that date and subsequently deposited the balance amount. After that, the auction sale was made final. 

 4. The judgment debtor-petitioner filed an application under Order 21 Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for setting aside the auction. They said was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 2005 which was dismissed by the order dated 20.11.2005. Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 2005 filed by the judgment- debtor-petitioner was also dismissed on the same date. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order dated 28.10.2007, auction purchaser-respondent No. 1 filed Writ Petition No. 10220 of 2007 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule Nisi. The High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 26.11.2008 made the Rule absolute and set aside the impugned judgment and order dated 28.10.2007 passed in Money Execution Case No. 142 of 2000. 

 9. Mr. Muhammad Jamiruddin Sarcar, learned Counsel for the review petitioner, A submits that section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2009 is independent of the provision of Order 21 Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure and that the executing Court rightly exercised its discretion in setting aside the auction sale and that the high Court Division without taking into consideration this legal aspect of the case made the Rule absolute upholding the auction sale and that this Division also approved the decision of the High Court Division without at all considering this legal aspect of the case and as such, the impugned judgment should be reviewed. 

 11. From the aforesaid findings, it appears that the review petitioner also invoked section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 2005 filed on 25.08.2005. The Artha Rin Adalat dismissed that miscellaneous case by the judgment and order dated 20.11.2005. Record reveals that the review petitioner again filed an application under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 praying for setting aside the auction sale which was allowed. 

 13. The points raised in the instant petition for review have already been addressed by this Division and as such, no interference is called for. In addition, the review petitioner could not make out a case for review of the impugned judgment as contemplated under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
